configurations.name: finatt-web
configurations.//: Plain `bash -c`, not `-lc`: a login shell runs profile scripts first and, when the launcher's inherited cwd is unreadable, floods stderr with getcwd/chdir errors that bury the real failure.
configurations.//autoPort: 3000 is held by the FinBud-LiveKit dev server, so take any free port. The dev script is `next dev -H 0.0.0.0` with no -p flag, which lets Next pick up the PORT env var the launcher assigns. NOTE: Supabase only redirects to allow-listed origins, so sign-in stays broken on a non-3000 port until NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and the Supabase redirect allowlist are updated to match.

configurations.name: finatt-app-web
configurations.//: This checkout. The `finatt-web` entry above points at the sibling ~/Downloads/FinAtt, which is what currently holds port 3000.
runtimeArgs: cd '/Users/rahul/Downloads/FinAtt app/frontend' && exec npm run dev

configurations.name: finatt-rn-web
configurations.//: The Expo app on its React Native Web target. Lets the splash animation and auth screens be checked in a browser without Xcode or an Android emulator.
runtimeArgs: cd '/Users/rahul/Downloads/FinAtt app/mobile-rn' && exec npx expo start --web --port $PORT

configurations.name: finatt-rn-dist
configurations.//: Serves the PRODUCTION web export from mobile-rn/dist, so `npm run build:web` output can be checked before it goes to Firebase Hosting. Dev-server success does not prove the production bundle boots.
